doc.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: Sicilian family, Tarrytown, and father the shoemaker
summary: Family came from Sicily via New Jersey to Tarrytown; relatives at General Motors, father a shoemaker.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I’ve been looking forward to this time. I understand that your family came over from Sicily.
Did they settle right here in Tarrytown?
Yeah, they made a stop maybe in Elizabeth, New Jersey, some people that came over, and then they settled right here, settled in Tarrytown, all my relatives, everybody.
What was the family business for you as you grew up? Your parents were—

Uh, family business, it was big family and there was a number of businesses. My grandfather in Sicily, which I never met, was superintendent of the sulfur mines in Sicily, where the ball is. You know Ragusa was right on the ball. There’s the boot and then there’s the ball. They were right across from Tunisia. And most of the relatives all worked in General Motors here in Tarrytown. They worked in General Motors. Now they’re breaking it down, they’re breaking General Motors down, but this was the big thing in town, this was the big money maker, so that’s it. And my father, he made shoes and fixed shoes. So that’s where I got my soul.
Oh, good one — very good one, I like that.
Yeah now he was a shoemaker but he started working at General Motors because they all did you know.
